verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED. Nothing is missing and nothing is misquoted about the text; the only alleged defect is markdown '#' depth, which is formatting the PDF does not encode.

(1) Every heading is PRESENT in the markdown with its exact number and exact title. Rendered p567 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v567/spec_p567.png) prints, in order: '14.6.2  State of a function, method, object, or program', '14.6.2.1  General', '14.6.2.2  Active state', '14.6.2.3  Initial and last-used states of data', '14.6.2.3.1  General'. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 23715, 23718, 23723, 23742, 23745 carry all five verbatim, each with an anchor (section-14-6-2 ... section-14-6-2-3-1). The claim's own 'markdown_says' quotes them, so the claim concedes no heading is missing - the kind label 'missing-heading' is a misnomer for what is actually a heading-DEPTH complaint. All intervening body text on the page (the run-unit/non-COBOL implementor paragraph, the three 'An instance of a function/method/program' paragraphs, the three-item em-dash list, the 'Whenever an instance...' paragraph, and the INITIALIZE NOTE) is also present and unaltered.

(2) The PDF supplies NO typographic level signal for the markdown to have lost. I rendered the sibling page 566 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v566/spec_p566.png) to check: '14.6  Execution' and '14.6.1  Run unit organization' are set in the SAME bold face at the SAME point size as '14.6.2', '14.6.2.1', '14.6.2.2', '14.6.2.3' and '14.6.2.3.1' on page 567. ISO/IEC 1989:2023 distinguishes clause depth exclusively by the dotted number, not by type. That number is transcribed exactly, so the hierarchy is fully recoverable from the markdown text itself; the '#' count carries no information the PDF ever asserted. This is 'only formatting' in the strict sense: a reader or tool derives 14.6.2's parentage from '14.6.2', not from '##'.

(3) The depth flattening is a document-wide convention artifact, not a page-567 event. Within the same clause the transcription emits '## 14.6.2.3.2 Initial state', '## 14.6.2.3.3 Last-used state', '## 14.6.2.4 Initial state of object data', '## 14.6.9.4 Space filling a dynamic table', '## 14.6.13.1 Exception conditions' and '## 14.6.13.1.1 General' - four- and five-level clauses also pinned at '##'. The same pattern runs through '## 14.2.2 Syntax rules', '## 14.5.2 Conditional phrase', '## 14.7.1 General'. The transcription simply never nests deeper than a shallow cap and resets to '##' at arbitrary points; singling out 14.6.2 as a page-specific structural regression misrepresents a global rendering habit as a localized transcription error.

No semantics, no syntax, no general rule, and no citable text differs between the PDF and the markdown on this page. Nothing about INITIAL programs, active state, or initial/last-used data state is affected: 14.6.2.1-14.6.2.3.1 are all present, correctly numbered, and complete.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. All five clause headings on page 567 (14.6.2, 14.6.2.1, 14.6.2.2, 14.6.2.3, 14.6.2.3.1) and all of the page's body text are present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md verbatim and correctly numbered. The claim reduces to markdown heading-depth ('##' vs '###'), which the PDF does not encode - pages 566 and 567 print 14.6, 14.6.1, 14.6.2, 14.6.2.1 and 14.6.2.3.1 in identical bold type at identical size, with depth conveyed solely by the dotted number that the transcription preserves. The flattening is moreover systemic across the whole file (e.g. '## 14.6.2.3.2', '## 14.6.2.4', '## 14.6.13.1.1', '## 14.2.2'), not a defect introduced on this page. At most this is a cosmetic, document-wide outline-normalization nit; it is not a page-567 structural finding and does not belong in the reconciliation ledger.
